subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should `message(action="send")` ignore or strip content-bearing poll params when the user asked for a normal send, or should those fields remain a hard fail-closed signal until schemas are split by action/channel?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats `pollQuestion` and `pollOption` as poll intent, while the report and linked PRs argue that schema-filled poll fields should not block ordinary sends; automation should not choose that shared tool contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow the send contract
options.body: Strip or hide poll creation fields for `action="send"`, preserve `action="poll"` validation, and require regression plus live delivery proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep fail-closed poll intent
options.body: Leave content-bearing poll fields as a hard `send` error and document that callers must avoid those fields or use model/tool routing that does not overfill them.

options.title: Defer to schema split
options.body: Pause narrow runtime fixes and design per-action or per-channel message schemas before changing the shared guard semantics.

recommendation.title: Narrow the send contract
recommendation.body: Strip or hide poll creation fields for `action="send"`, preserve `action="poll"` validation, and require regression plus live delivery proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent current-main history attributes the active narrowed guard behavior to this area owner signal, while the choice is a shared product/tool contract decision.
